items.stimulus: וְלָאָרֶץ לֹא יְכֻפַּר לַדָּם אֲשֶׁר שֻׁפַּךְ בָּהּ כִּי אִם בְּדַם שֹׁפְכוֹ
options: The heavens are telling the glory of God.
And Pharaoh called all the wise men of Egypt, and he related to them his dream.
Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy.
And no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that has been shed in it, except by the blood of him that shed it.
items.answer: And no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that has been shed in it, except by the blood of him that shed it.

source.citation: Davidson, An Introductory Hebrew Grammar (22nd ed., 1923), exercise §26 A 7; McFadyen, Key to the Exercises (1924)
source.note: Transcribed by hand from the scans and checked against the Key.

items.stimulus: וְהָלְכוּ יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ כַּעִוְרִים וְשֻׁפַּךְ דָּמָם כֶּעָפָר
options: The Israelites ate the passover with their loins girt, their sandals on their feet, and their staff in their hand.
And the inhabitants of the land shall go (i.e. walk) like blind men, and their blood shall be poured out like dust.
And ye shall take your staff in your hand.
items.answer: And the inhabitants of the land shall go (i.e. walk) like blind men, and their blood shall be poured out like dust.

source.citation: Davidson, An Introductory Hebrew Grammar (22nd ed., 1923), exercise §30 B 5; McFadyen, Key to the Exercises (1924)
